about: Command-line tasks of 2026-11-22, written and committed before any run. A tester is shown only `words`, in a folder made by make-cli-folder.mjs from `source`. `rightAnswer` is for the judge only. The first five are the page testers' tasks (AI-Agent-Workspace/scripts/playtest/tasks.json, same ids) reworded for a folder in place of a link, their keys carried over and adapted where the page's condition does not hold; the last three are new, of the kind the command line should be best at, their keys written from the source: estate-dead by reading the estate's files, repo-reach and repo-touch from TypeScript's own module resolution (import-oracle.mjs beside this file, run at 64ab0ed54).

tasks.words: A colleague pointed me to one of the files in our payments code, Contracts/IPaymentService.cs. What uses this file?
tasks.rightAnswer: Carried from tasks.json. Contracts/IPaymentService.cs is used by four files: Hub/PaymentHub.cs and PaymentService/PaymentService.cs (code), and Hub/App.config and PaymentService/App.config (configuration that names the service contract). Right: the two code files and the two configuration files. Partly: the code files alone. Wrong: a file named that does not use it, or neither code file.

tasks.words: Can you look at the PaymentService folder and tell me how the files in it connect?
tasks.rightAnswer: Carried from tasks.json, less its sentence on finding the World Map's box. PaymentService/ holds App.config, PaymentService.cs, PaymentService.csproj and a Data/ subfolder (Payment.cs, PaymentsContext.cs, PostPaymentRow.cs). Inside: PaymentService.cs uses Payment.cs, PostPaymentRow.cs and PaymentsContext.cs; PaymentsContext.cs uses Payment.cs, PostPaymentRow.cs and App.config (its PaymentsDb connection string); App.config names PaymentService.cs as the service, which closes a cycle PaymentService.cs -> PaymentsContext.cs -> App.config -> PaymentService.cs; PaymentService.csproj connects to nothing inside the folder. Outside: PaymentService.cs uses four Contracts files (IPaymentService, PaymentQuery, PaymentRequest, PaymentResult); App.config names Contracts/IPaymentService.cs and is used by Hub/App.config; Payment.cs and PaymentsContext.cs reach the SQL Server scripts; the .csproj references Contracts.csproj. Right: the inside connections with their directions and PaymentService.cs as the hub; the cycle and the outside connections are a plus. Partly: the files listed with some connections, or directions missing. Wrong: files invented or the connections contradicted.

tasks.words: This folder holds our payments system. When someone submits a payment on the web page, what happens to it? Name each piece of the system it passes through, in order, until it is stored.
tasks.rightAnswer: Carried from tasks.json. A full answer names, in this order, Portal/Pages/Default.aspx and Portal/Scripts/portal.js, the portal's Portal/Controllers/PaymentsController.cs and Portal/Services/GatewayClient.cs, the gateway (Gateway/Controllers/PaymentsController.cs and Gateway/Wcf/HubProxy.cs, over the endpoint PaymentHub in Gateway/Web.config), the hub (Hub/PaymentHub.cs with Hub/ServiceRouting.cs, endpoints in Hub/App.config), the payment service PaymentService/PaymentService.cs and its PaymentService/Data/PaymentsContext.cs, the stored procedure Database/SqlServer/dbo.usp_PostPayment.sql, and the table dbo.Payment (Database/SqlServer/dbo.Payment.sql); the Oracle read of CENTRAL.ACCOUNT through ORACLE_CENTRAL and the configuration files that carry each hop are a plus. Partly: the right order with a piece missing or merged (the portal's own controller skipped, the hub's routing not named, or the answer stopping at the service or the database without the table). Wrong: an order that contradicts the flow, or the payment said to be stored somewhere else.

tasks.words: Nothing in our C# code ever creates a PaymentHub (the class in Hub/PaymentHub.cs). Is it dead code that we can delete?
tasks.rightAnswer: Written 2026-11-22 from the estate's files, before any run. No. Hub/App.config hosts it: `<service name="Estate.Hub.PaymentHub">` with its endpoint at net.tcp://hub.onprem.example:8731/PaymentHub, so the WCF host creates it from configuration, not code. The gateway calls it: Gateway/Wcf/HubProxy.cs opens the client endpoint "PaymentHub" of Gateway/Web.config, whose address is that same net.tcp://hub.onprem.example:8731/PaymentHub, and every payment posted through the portal passes through PaymentHub on its way to the payment service (it asks Hub/ServiceRouting.cs for the endpoint and forwards the call). Right: no, naming the hosting by Hub/App.config's service entry, or the gateway's call to it over that address (both are a plus). Partly: no, with a reason that names neither (it implements IPaymentHub, it might be used by reflection, it is in the solution). Wrong: yes, or safe to delete, or no answer.
